scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the safe installation requirements, structural and ventilation guidelines, and mechanical limits for gas-based instantaneous water heaters (gas geysers) and associated components—including gas piping, regulators, hoses, and venting systems—to prevent toxic combustion product accumulation (carbon monoxide) and fire hazards in residential, commercial, or institutional properties.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural Code of Practice / Safety and Installation Guidelines (Mechanical Engineering Department / Domestic Gas Appliances)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Mandatory Procedural Compliance. Under the Gas Cylinder Rules of the Government of India and local public utility regulations (including IGL, MNGL, and state gas distribution agencies), domestic and commercial piping installations must hold a valid certificate of compliance (CoC) issued by an authorized contractor, verifying strict adherence to the safety, ventilation, and zoning codes of IS 16093.

requirements.detail: Prescribes requirements for installing gas-based instantaneous water heaters, as well as the associated components like piping and mechanical fittings.

Installing flue-less gas instantaneous water heaters inside closed bathrooms or shower stalls is strictly prohibited due to the critical risk of rapid oxygen depletion, incomplete combustion, and fatal carbon monoxide (CO) accumulation.

Gas geysers must not be concealed inside solid wood cabinetry, cupboards, or closets without non-closable ventilation openings, to prevent dangerous accumulations of unburnt fuel gas or exhaust fumes.

Highly recommends utilizing balanced-flue (room-sealed) gas geysers, where combustion air is drawn exclusively from outside the building envelope and exhaust gases are vented directly back to the outside.

Where a non-balanced flue heater is installed in semi-enclosed spaces or kitchens, a permanent, non-closable fresh air ventilation opening of at least 45 cm x 45 cm (2025 sq. cm) leading to the outside must be provided.
All installed domestic gas geysers must hold valid BIS licenses conforming to the manufacturing specifications and safety features of IS 15558.
LPG geysers must operate under a nominal regulated water/gas stabilizer working pressure of 21 mbar (g) or 30 gf/cm² (2.942 kN/m²).
All intermediate copper tubing connecting the low-pressure regulator manifold to the geyser gas inlet must utilize high-conductivity seamless pipes conforming to IS 2501.
Flexible connections must utilize synthetic rubber hoses conforming strictly to IS 9573 (Type I/II) or IS 10908, showing zero kinks, weathering, or cracks.

Site operators must check all flexible rubber hose ends, copper fittings, and regulator bungs weekly using a soap-water solution, prohibiting the use of open flames or running the appliance if gas smell is detected.

Observed or calculated dimensions, clearances, test pressures, and gas concentrations must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16093 : 2013 is the primary national Indian Standard code of practice establishing the mandatory safety, architectural, and mechanical requirements for the installation of gas-based instantaneous water heaters (gas geysers). Formulated under the Domestic and Commercial Gas Burning Appliances Sectional Committee (MED 23) and reaffirmed in 2023, the standard addresses critical safety challenges in residential and commercial buildings. It strictly prohibits installing flue-less gas water heaters inside closed bathrooms or unventilated cupboards to prevent fatal carbon monoxide poisoning (known as gas geyser syndrome). It mandates the use of highly secure, balanced-flue systems or the provision of large (min. 45 x 45 cm) permanent fresh-air ventilation openings leading directly to the outer atmosphere, while regulating all gas-carrying copper tubes, regulators, and synthetic rubber hoses to ensure gas-tightness and prevent explosions.
